title: Cylindrical object
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to -90.0 degrees around the x-axis, 0.0 degrees around the y-axis, and -90.0 degrees around the z-axis. Ensure the translation vector is set to (0.0, 0.0, 0.0). Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on a new face. In this first face, draw a single loop, and within this loop, draw a circle with its center at (0.05, 0.05) and a radius of 0.05. Apply a scaling factor of 0.1 to the two-dimensional sketch. Transform the two-dimensional sketch into three dimensions by rotating it using the Euler angles (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and translating it using the translation vector (0.0, 0.0, 0.0). Extrude the two-dimensional sketch to create a three-dimensional model. Set the extrusion depth towards the normal to 0.75 and the extrusion depth opposite the normal to 0.0. Finally, create a new solid body from this extrusion. The final cylindrical object will have a length of 0.1, a width of 0.1, and a height of 0.75.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a circle with the specified center and radius
r = r.center(0.05, 0.05).circle(0.05)

# Extrude the circle to create a cylinder
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90, 0, -90) and the translation vector is (0, 0, 0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the cylinder 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90).rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the circle for the base of the cylinder
r = r.center(0.05, 0.05).circle(0.05)

# Extrude the circle to create the cylinder
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
# The translation vector is [0, 0, 0], so no translation is needed
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90).rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

lanes.label: Cadabra 4B (ours) · 1 sample
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the circle for the sketch
circle_center = (0.05, 0.05)
circle_radius = 0.05

# Create the sketch on the XY plane
r = r.center(*circle_center).circle(circle_radius)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
extrude_depth = 0.75

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90, 0, -90) and the translation vector is (0, 0, 0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the cylinder 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.extrude(extrude_depth).rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90).rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)
